steps: Pick a team name and create a folder named after it at the top level of the hackathon repo.
Add a README.md with what you built, what problem it solves, and how you built it with Claude Code.
Commit your working code, skill, plugin, or MCP config into that folder.
Record a short screen-capture demo (about 2-3 minutes) and link it from your README.
Push to github.com/gatesfoundation/gf-claude-hackathon-2026 before the 2:10 PM PT deadline.
Confirm your push landed by reloading the repo in a browser, then take the break.
If you are shortlisted as a finalist, be ready to demo live for about 4 minutes.
submission.fallback: If you cannot push to GitHub (no repo access, non-technical registrant, or a virtual participant hitting auth issues), do not spend build time fighting it. Zip your project folder plus your README and screen capture, and ask a floor helper how to get it in before 2:10 PM PT. Sharing the zip over Teams was raised as a likely fallback route but is not confirmed policy, so check with a helper or the MC rather than assuming.

faq.q: Claude Desktop will not reinstall from the company portal
faq.a: A known issue today — isDesktopExtensionEnabled stays at 0. Ask Andy Stetzler at table 4 or Brian Munn at table 6 rather than burning build time on it.

faq.q: My team is virtual — is there a breakout room for us?
faq.a: No. Start your own Teams meeting with your team and drop back into the main meeting for the checkpoints. The pre-created breakout rooms are not being used. Ping the main chat any time you need help — support is monitoring it.

faq.q: I have no audio in the Teams meeting — what do I do?
faq.a: Join from Chrome instead. Several people hit this at kickoff and switching browsers fixed it immediately.

faq.q: How big should a team be?
faq.a: Two people is the default. Three or four is fine if that is what your group wants - just be honest about whether four people can stay busy in a short build window. Solo is allowed but pairing is strongly encouraged: put an experienced Claude Code user with a newcomer.

faq.q: I do not have a team. What do I do?
faq.a: Come to the team formation and scoping block and say so - the MC will pair you up, and pods are assigned by table stand. Virtual participants should say the same in the Teams channel and a helper will match you. Nobody needs to arrive with a team.

faq.q: How do I submit my project?
faq.a: Push to github.com/gatesfoundation/gf-claude-hackathon-2026 by 2:10 PM PT: a folder named for your team, a README describing what you built and what it solves, your code or skill or MCP config, and a link to a short screen-capture demo. Written submissions plus the screen capture are what the judges shortlist from - only 6 to 8 finalists demo live.

faq.q: What if I cannot push to GitHub?
faq.a: Do not burn build time on it. Zip your project folder with your README and screen capture, and ask a floor helper how to get it submitted before the deadline. Sharing it over Teams was discussed as a likely fallback for non-technical registrants but is not confirmed policy, so check with a helper rather than assuming.

Memphis Smokehouse buffet, served outside the room, open from 11:45 AM to 2:00 PM. Beverages are inside the room. You can grab food and keep building - the buffet stays open through most of the build window.

faq.q: Who do I ask for help?
faq.a: Floor helpers are circulating all day for build, install, and auth questions - flag one down rather than getting stuck. Virtual participants should post in the monitored Teams channel. For registration, AV, or room logistics, go to the registration desk or the MC.

Four equally weighted criteria, 25% each: Real-Work Impact (solves a real problem here and fits a problem statement), Staying Power (you and your colleagues will actually keep using it - a reusable skill, agent, MCP integration, or workflow), Claude Code Craft (creative use of Claude Code beyond a single prompt), and Execution and Demo (sound engineering, refined past the first idea, a demo that holds up live). Finalist demos are hard-stopped by a timer, so rehearse the short version.

faq.q: The idea I want to build looks too big for the time. Should I still try?
faq.a: Scope it down deliberately. Real build time is under two hours, so the ideas that finish are skills and plugins - the email template customizer, agreement-readiness checklist, strategic-fit drafting skill, prompt variance injector. The knowledge-graph and benchmark-harness ideas are multi-day projects and will demo as a fragment. A narrow working thing beats a broad broken one on this rubric.

tips.detail: Ask Claude to interview you for intent before it writes anything. Plan first, then auto mode.
Around 30–40% of the context window Claude starts getting confused. Run /compact or hand off to a fresh session at that point rather than pushing through.
No carryover at all — you rely entirely on memory and CLAUDE.md. The scratchpad goes too.
It self-documents the project. Then tell Claude to record important changes and architectural shifts as you go.

tips.tip: Treat CLAUDE.md like onboarding a new hire
tips.detail: How to get started, decisions made, look and feel, standing rules — "always make pull requests", "keep a changelog", "never do X".

tips.tip: Make Claude verify its own work
tips.detail: /review is useful. Ask it to test what it built and loop until it passes, then test it yourself as a human.

tips.tip: Split big work into multiple plans
tips.detail: A fresh session with a tight context window beats one long confused one.
Give Claude a picture of your architecture sketch and ask for a design plan.
